summary: 4 orphan stores deleted (461 lines); index.ts never exported them (implementer claim verified); npm run build compiles successfully; grep returns zero matches in src/.

All acceptance criteria met; queue payload matches sister 5.1.3 (queue name 'send-campaign-email' identical, payload superset includes all 4 fields sister consumes); minor coordination + ergonomics issues only.

issues.problem: Producer exports CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_QUEUE_NAME / getCampaignEmailQueue / CampaignEmailJobData / campaignEmailJobId. Sister consumer 5.1.3 (src/workers/campaign-email-worker.ts) DOES NOT IMPORT from this file — it redeclares CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_QUEUE and CampaignEmailJobData locally. Queue name string matches ('send-campaign-email') so wiring works, and producer payload {campaign_id, recipient_id, customer_id, org_id, tracking_id} is a superset of consumer payload {campaign_id, recipient_id, tracking_id, org_id} so worker reads succeed. NOT a P0 — runtime integration is correct via shared queue name. But duplicated constants risk future drift.
issues.suggested_fix: In a follow-up cleanup task post-batch, refactor the worker to import CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_QUEUE_NAME and CampaignEmailJobData from src/lib/queue/campaign-email-queue.ts so producer is single source of truth.

issues.problem: MANAGER_ROLES bypass for PIN is unreachable in practice — requireRole already restricts callers to ['owner','admin','manager'], all of which are in MANAGER_ROLES. The PIN check therefore never executes for any current caller, defeating the requires_approval gate entirely (a manager can send a requires_approval campaign without entering a PIN).
issues.suggested_fix: Either narrow requireRole to ['staff','server','manager','admin','owner'] so non-managers can hit this endpoint and require PIN, OR drop the callerIsManager bypass so even managers must re-enter their own PIN for approval-gated campaigns. Spec implies the latter (manager-PIN audit-log entry per CLAUDE.md).

issues.problem: Audit-log row required by CLAUDE.md ('privileged actions ... require manager-PIN with audit log entry') is deferred — code captures approvingManagerId then voids it with a comment 'persisted in a sister batch'. Spec acceptance criteria for 5.1.2 includes Manager-PIN gate but does not explicitly include audit_log; reviewer flags as P2 deferred work to track.
issues.suggested_fix: Insert an audit_log row { actor_user_id: user.id, approving_manager_id, action: 'campaign.send', target_id: campaign.id } at the same point. Track in batch follow-up if intentionally deferred.

issues.problem: Hardcoded DEFAULT_MAX_RECIPIENTS = 50_000. For a single-restaurant POS this is fine, but a single 50k-recipient run will issue 50k addBulk Redis ops + 50k row inserts in one transaction; no batching/streaming. Acceptable for current customer base; risky at scale.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a batch loop (e.g. chunks of 1000) for both the upsert and addBulk in src/app/api/marketing/campaigns/[id]/send/route.ts when recipients.length > some threshold. Defer to a perf task.

summary: All acceptance criteria met (TODO@459 resolved, pure diff lib, ADD badge in UI, single org-scoped query, type aligned, build passes); P2 concerns: no unit tests for diff lib, and 5s anchor heuristic may misclassify if multiple original items are inserted across a slow round-trip.

issues.problem: Pure function with branchy logic and a magic threshold (ADD_WINDOW_MS=5000) ships without unit tests. Trivial to add — the spec's own checklist flags this as a good-to-have.
issues.suggested_fix: Add tests/lib/kds/diff.test.ts covering: (a) empty input, (b) all items within 5s -> no ADDs, (c) item 6s+ later -> flagged is_add, (d) void items ignored, (e) null sent_at ignored, (f) malformed sent_at falls back without throwing.

issues.problem: 5-second anchor heuristic is reasonable for the common case but is sent_at-batch sensitive. If the POS writes order_items.sent_at one row at a time over a slow connection (>5s spread across the original batch), the trailing rows of the original send will be falsely flagged as ADDs. The real signal (a separate add-items API call) is not used; sent_at clock skew is.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) widen ADD_WINDOW_MS to 30s to match human ADD cadence (a server walking back to the POS rarely takes <30s), or (b) better, add a dedicated column (e.g. order_items.send_batch_id or added_after_send boolean) populated by the add-items API so detection is exact rather than timing-inferred. Track as follow-up.

issues.problem: Second select on order_items duplicates work already done at line 169 for non-expo stations -- the route now does two .select() calls on order_items per request (one station-filtered, one unfiltered for diff anchoring). For 50 active orders this is acceptable but on a large floor with many station KDS terminals polling, the load doubles.
issues.suggested_fix: For expo stations (no prep_station filter), the first query already returns all items -- skip the 3b query and reuse `items`. For prep-station stations, the 3b query is needed; consider adding it as a second batch in a Promise.all with the events query (3) instead of awaiting serially.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria met; build passes; GIF valid; URL params align with sister 5.1.3 worker; P2 issues: read-then-write race on open/click counters, missing org_id scoping in getCampaignAnalytics (admin client bypasses RLS), three eslint-disables without tracking comments.

issues.problem: upsertOpen does read-then-write on open_count; two concurrent opens for the same tracking_id can both read N and both write N+1, undercounting by 1. Same pattern in upsertClick (line 170).
issues.suggested_fix: Use a Supabase RPC with `update campaign_recipients set open_count = open_count + 1, opened_at = coalesce(opened_at, now()) where tracking_id = $1` for atomicity. Low-stakes for email telemetry but flagged.

issues.problem: getCampaignAnalytics uses admin client (bypasses RLS) but does NOT filter by org_id — only by campaign_id. Caller is expected to scope but signature does not enforce it. CLAUDE.md mandates org_id on every query.
issues.suggested_fix: Add required `org_id: string` parameter and add `.eq('org_id', org_id)` to the select chain so cross-tenant leak is impossible from any caller.

issues.problem: Three `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` directives without accompanying TODO + tracking task ID (reviewer protocol requirement).
issues.suggested_fix: Add `// TODO(5.x): replace with generated Supabase types` next to each disable, or generate types and remove the casts.

summary: Worker compiles and structure is sound but two P0s block production: customers.unsubscribe_token does not exist in baseline so 100% of jobs will throw and mark recipients failed; backoff strategy mismatch with sister 5.1.2 producer means specified 5s/30s/5min retry timing is never applied (producer enqueues with type:exponential, worker's custom strategy is dead code).

issues.problem: Worker selects customers.unsubscribe_token but the column does not exist in supabase/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql (customers schema lines 575-598). Sister 5.1.2 migration (20260504005008_add_campaign_recipients_indexes.sql) only touches campaign_recipients and campaigns. Every job will fail with 'column customers.unsubscribe_token does not exist', exhaust 3 retries, and mark recipient status='failed'. Zero emails will ship.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) add a customers.unsubscribe_token column in a new migration in this branch (text, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text, with backfill for existing rows); or (b) coordinate with runner to add a sister task before integration. Option (a) preferred — the worker already treats token absence as a hard fail.

issues.problem: Backoff mismatch with sister 5.1.2 producer. Producer (campaign-email-queue.ts:68-73) sets defaultJobOptions.backoff={type:'exponential',delay:5000}. Worker registers settings.backoffStrategy=campaignEmailBackoff (custom 5s/30s/5min) but BullMQ only invokes a custom strategy when the job's own backoff.type === 'custom'. Producer never sets type:'custom', so retries will be exponential (5s/10s/20s), violating the spec's 5s/30s/5min requirement.
issues.suggested_fix: Either: (a) producer should import CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_JOB_OPTS from campaign-email-worker (or a shared module) and pass it via Queue.add opts so type:'custom' is set per-job; or (b) consolidate queue config in src/lib/queue/campaign-email-queue.ts as the single source of truth and have producer use defaultJobOptions={attempts:3, backoff:{type:'custom', delay:5000}} — then worker's settings.backoffStrategy will fire. Suggest option (b) and have worker import queue name + types from the shared queue lib.

issues.problem: CampaignEmailJobData interface is redefined locally with shape {campaign_id, recipient_id, tracking_id, org_id} while sister 5.1.2 (src/lib/queue/campaign-email-queue.ts:23) exports an interface of the SAME name with shape {campaign_id, recipient_id, customer_id, org_id, tracking_id} — adds customer_id. Two modules will export an identically named interface. Worker re-fetches customer_id from campaign_recipients so runtime is unaffected, but consumers that import the wrong one will silently get the wrong shape.
issues.suggested_fix: Delete the local interface in campaign-email-worker.ts and import { CampaignEmailJobData, CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_QUEUE_NAME } from '@/lib/queue/campaign-email-queue'. Replace local CAMPAIGN_EMAIL_QUEUE constant with the imported name.

issues.problem: buildUnsubscribeUrl points to /api/marketing/unsubscribe?t={token} but no sister task in batch 5.1 implements that route (verified in v5-batch-5.1-tracking — only /track/open and /track/click exist). Every email's unsubscribe link will 404 in production. Violates Rule 18 (lying buttons) and breaks RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post one-click — Gmail/Apple Mail will POST to the 404 endpoint and may flag the sender domain.
issues.suggested_fix: Recommend runner option (c): add a sister task to batch 5.1 (or insert a 5.1.5 stub) that builds POST+GET /api/marketing/unsubscribe handler which (1) looks up customer by unsubscribe_token, (2) sets marketing_opt_in=false, (3) returns 200 with confirmation page. Until that lands, FAIL this task — shipping a 404 unsubscribe link will torch sender reputation in days.

issues.problem: createAdminClient() is called inside the 'failed' event listener for every failed job. Depending on createAdminClient's implementation this may open a new HTTP/Postgres connection per failure event under retry storms.
issues.suggested_fix: Hoist a single admin client to module scope or inside startCampaignEmailWorker and reuse it for the failed-listener path.

issues.problem: Idempotency guard short-circuits only on status==='sent'. A re-enqueue for a recipient already in 'bounced' or 'failed' state will re-render and re-send. Producer's deterministic jobId protects in normal flow but a manual re-enqueue (admin retry, ops script) would re-send.
issues.suggested_fix: Extend the guard: if (['sent','bounced'].includes(recipient.status)) return skipped. Failed status is intentionally retryable from ops, leave it.

issues.problem: customers select doesn't fetch last_name even though the spec calls for personalized greeting. Acceptable since template uses first_name only, but org_logo_url and mailing_address are read from organizations table without verifying those columns exist in baseline schema (worker falls back gracefully so no runtime crash, but if the columns truly don't exist the SELECT itself errors before the fallback).
issues.suggested_fix: Verify organizations table has logo_url and mailing_address columns (grep baseline). If not, narrow the SELECT to columns that exist or wrap in a try/catch that falls back to {name: orgId}.

summary: Cycle 2 fixes verified: unsubscribe_token migration correct, manual backoff loop properly re-enqueues with delay+unique jobId+attempts:1, unsubscribe endpoint is RFC8058-compliant + Zod-validated + tenant-scoped + idempotent.

issues.problem: Multiple eslint-disable any-casts on Supabase client because regenerated types do not yet include unsubscribe_token
issues.suggested_fix: After merge + supabase types regen, drop the any casts.

issues.problem: completed listener logs status='retried' as if successful which could confuse on-call
issues.suggested_fix: Log retried status at warn level or distinguish the event.

summary: org_processor_bindings migration + rollback meet all acceptance criteria; immutability trigger uses check_violation ERRCODE, RLS is SELECT-only, backfill is idempotent, rollback drops in correct dep order.

All 9 acceptance criteria met; build + lint clean; processor-locked framework, registry, scanners, drivers, and 2 API routes implemented to spec with proper fallbacks for missing sister-task migration.

issues.problem: Sister UI worktree (5.2.0c) calls GET /api/payments/processor-binding to fetch the read-only 'Bound to: Valor' badge data, but this endpoint was not created in 5.2.0b. UI has a graceful fallback to literal 'valor' on 404, and since Processor type is a const literal 'valor', the fallback is correctness-equivalent. Recommend adding a thin GET route in a follow-up batch (or letting the UI hardcode 'valor' permanently).
issues.suggested_fix: Add src/app/api/payments/processor-binding/route.ts with GET that calls getProcessorBinding(user.org_id) and returns {data: {processor: binding.processor}}; or remove the UI fetch entirely and hardcode 'valor' since the type permits no other value.

issues.problem: Multiple eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any comments without TODO+tracker references. Project rule (CLAUDE.md + reviewer protocol) requires eslint-disable to be paired with a TODO. However, this exact pattern (untyped Supabase client casts) is the established convention in this codebase (see src/app/api/orders/[id]/walkout/route.ts:48,68,104,133,151), so it does not represent a new project-rule violation introduced by this batch.
issues.suggested_fix: No action needed for this PR; tracked separately as the project-wide Supabase typing TODO. Consider adding a single repo-wide TODO comment in src/lib/supabase/admin.ts referencing the gen-types task.

issues.problem: Dynamic import uses /* webpackIgnore: true */ — a webpack-specific magic comment that has no effect under Turbopack (Next 16 default). Behavior is still correct (try/catch swallows missing-module errors), but the comment is misleading.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the /* webpackIgnore: true */ comment, or replace with a brief inline comment explaining the optional-dep pattern.

summary: All 10 acceptance criteria met; build + lint clean (zero new warnings); processor field is read-only Badge with Lock icon (zero <select>/<input> matches); ManagerPinDialog imported from canonical /pos path; Badge variants additive (success/warning) — no breaking change to existing variants; Rule-18 compliant (no Actions menu rendered, all rendered actions hit real APIs); 404 fallback on /api/payments/processor-binding fires cleanly to 'valor' default with try/catch wrapper.

issues.problem: File is 707 lines, exceeding the project's 500-line guideline. New file in this branch (not preserved V4 code as report claimed — git shows it as A/added). Tabs the workstation pairing flow into terminals page is fine functionally; size is purely a cleanup opportunity.
issues.suggested_fix: Extract subcomponents (PairingDialog, RoleSheet, TerminalRow) into sibling files under src/components/settings/workstations/ in a follow-up. Non-blocking.

issues.problem: useEffect at line 122-132 starts the manager-PIN flow whenever open && scanState==='idle'. If the user cancels the PIN dialog (via overlay click), handlePinDialogChange closes the parent dialog only when scanState==='awaiting_pin' — correct — but a fast double-open of the parent could race the state reset. Low likelihood; current code paths are correct.
issues.suggested_fix: Consider gating the PIN auto-trigger on a separate ref-flag instead of scanState to make intent explicit. Optional polish.

issues.problem: fetchHardwareTerminals swallows non-OK responses and renders empty silently — acceptable for the dev/null-API case but masks real 500s from a future bug. No user-visible error toast.
issues.suggested_fix: Distinguish 404 (treat as empty) from 5xx (show error state with retry); current behavior is non-blocking but degrades observability when the API breaks.

summary: Build/lint clean and e2e demonstrates queue mechanics, but the new mutation_queue is a parallel, disconnected duplicate of the existing sync_queue infra — sister 5.3.2 wires its UI to sync_queue (zero overlap with 5.3.1's queue), no order/payment route enqueues into the new queue, and no API route honors Idempotency-Key (server dedupe is only mocked in the test).

issues.problem: Parallel queue infrastructure: this file + src/lib/offline/sync.ts + the new mutation_queue Dexie table duplicate the existing src/lib/offline/sync-queue.ts (with enqueueSync/getPendingCount/getPendingEntries) plus order-sync.ts/payment-sync.ts already in main. Sister 5.3.2 (worktree v5-batch-5.3.2-offline-ui) imports useSyncQueue and getPendingEntries from the EXISTING sync-queue.ts — its badge counter and drawer will never see entries enqueued via the new enqueueMutation API. After both merges land, mutations buffered through 5.3.1 will be invisible to the UI and will only be replayed by the new sync.ts (which no production code path calls).
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) extend the existing sync-queue.ts to add the UUIDv4 idempotency key column on sync_queue and an Idempotency-Key-aware replayer, dropping the new mutation_queue table + queue.ts + sync.ts entirely; or (b) have 5.3.2 re-target the new APIs and migrate existing order/payment/clock enqueuers to enqueueMutation. Option (a) is the smaller diff and avoids forking the offline subsystem.

issues.problem: No /api/orders or /api/payments route reads or honors the Idempotency-Key header. The acceptance criterion 'on reconnect, FIFO replay with Idempotency-Key header; server dedupes; no dupes' is not satisfied end-to-end — the server side of the contract does not exist. The e2e test only passes because page.route() supplies a fake seenKeys Set that pretends to dedupe. In production, two replays of the same key would create two orders.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a thin Idempotency-Key middleware (e.g. src/lib/api/idempotency.ts) that, for any mutating route, checks an idempotency_responses table keyed by (org_id, key) — return cached response on a hit, persist response on a fresh insert. Wire into orders/payments/comp/void/refund routes. Without this the queue replay is unsafe across any retry scenario, not just the offline reconnect path.

issues.problem: No production caller. grep across src/app/api, src/lib/orders, src/lib/payments shows zero invocations of enqueueMutation outside the test harness exposed on window. The 'mutations buffered to IndexedDB when offline' criterion is only true if the operator drives the queue via window.useOfflineStore — no real POS code path enqueues through it. Order/payment optimistic creates currently still go through the older sync-queue path.
issues.suggested_fix: Either fold this into the existing sync-queue (see P0 above) or, at minimum, wire src/lib/orders/* and src/lib/payments/* mutation entry points to enqueue via the new API when offline (and drop the older sync-queue once parity is reached).

issues.problem: Test-harness exposure (window.useOfflineStore + window.offlineDB) is gated only by NODE_ENV !== 'production'. Acceptable, but the offline UI in 5.3.2 will not exercise this path — recommend documenting that the only consumer is the e2e spec, or moving the harness into the spec via page.addInitScript so it doesn't ship in dev/preview builds either.
issues.suggested_fix: Move window assignments into a Playwright fixture (page.addInitScript) so non-prod builds don't expose internals to dev tools.

summary: All acceptance criteria met (badge+drawer+retry+abandon+manager-PIN+44px touch); build passes, 0 new lint errors; one P1 cross-task integration gap with 5.3.1.

issues.problem: Drawer reads from the legacy sync_queue (via useSyncQueue + sync-queue.ts). Sister task 5.3.1 introduced an independent mutation_queue (src/lib/offline/queue.ts + src/lib/offline/sync.ts + offline-store.pendingMutations) that this drawer does not surface. After both branches merge, mutations queued by 5.3.1 will not appear in the badge/drawer. No runtime crash — both queues coexist — but the user-visible 'pending' count omits 5.3.1 entries.
issues.suggested_fix: Follow-up task: union both queues. Either (a) extend useSyncQueue to also read from offline-store.pendingMutations + offline-store.actions.retryMutation/discardMutation, OR (b) collapse the two queues into one in a future refactor. Current implementation is acceptable for 5.3.2's scope as written but should be tracked as a known integration gap before 5.3 ships.

issues.problem: useEffect refresh polls only via the failedEntries.length dep + initial open. Pending entries that change (e.g. new queue inserts mid-drawer-open) won't appear until failedEntries changes or drawer reopens. The 5s poll inside useSyncQueue will trigger updates but only because failedEntries identity changes; pure-pending churn (no failures) won't refresh the list while the drawer is open.
issues.suggested_fix: Subscribe to onQueueChange directly inside the drawer to refresh when any entry mutates, not only when failedEntries changes.

summary: Cycle 2 fixes both P0s end-to-end: parallel queue infrastructure deleted (no queue.ts/sync.ts in src/lib/offline/), single canonical sync-queue.ts extended with UUIDv4 idempotency-key minting + getIdempotencyKey helper; all 4 replayer paths (order-sync, payment-sync, clock-sync, sync-processor) stamp Idempotency-Key header from entry; new src/lib/api/idempotency.ts middleware validates UUIDv4, dedupes by (key, route, org_id), caches 2xx+4xx but not 5xx, no-header passthrough preserved; 5 routes wrapped (POST /api/orders, PATCH /api/orders/[id], POST /api/orders/[id]/items, POST /api/payments/process, PATCH /api/tables/[id]); migration creates idempotency_records with composite PK, 24h TTL default, expires_at + org_id indexes, RLS enabled, paired rollback in supabase/_rollbacks/; sister 5.3.2 hook signature {pendingCount, pendingByType, failedEntries, conflicts, isSyncing, syncProgress, lastSyncAt} + retryEntry/removeEntry/getPendingEntries exports preserved; e2e suite has client-contract + real-API dedup + UUIDv4 negative; npm run build passes; npm run lint zero new errors.

issues.problem: Stale doc comment references deleted src/lib/offline/queue.ts (cycle 1 file removed in cycle 2 revert)
issues.suggested_fix: Update comment to reference src/lib/offline/sync-queue.ts (the canonical queue)

issues.problem: Test-harness exposes useOfflineStore/offlineDB/syncQueue/syncProcessor on window in non-prod via lazy dynamic import; relies on process.env.NODE_ENV stripping in prod build
issues.suggested_fix: Confirm Next.js DCE removes the test-harness branch in production bundles (verified by build); add an explicit NEXT_PUBLIC_TEST_HARNESS gate if extra defense-in-depth is desired

issues.problem: Uses createAdminClient (service-role) for cache lookup AND insert; the lookup itself bypasses RLS so the org_id equality filter is the only tenant guard — correct, but worth a comment-level callout
issues.suggested_fix: No code change needed; document is already clear that RLS is defense-in-depth. Optional: assert response_status >= 200 before caching to skip 1xx (currently caches 2xx + 3xx + 4xx via the !>=500 guard)

summary: Acceptance criteria met locally and 7/7 unit tests pass, but the audit.record signature exported by 5.4.3 is incompatible with sister 5.4.2 call sites — merge of both batches will not compile.

issues.problem: audit.record(input: AuditRecordInput) takes a single object argument with `actor: {id,email,org_id,role}`, `manager_pin_user_id`, and a narrow AuditAction union. Sister 5.4.2 calls `audit.record(supabase, {org_id, location_id, user_id, approved_by_user_id, action, ...})` at three sites: ../v5-batch-5.4.2-state-machine/src/app/api/orders/[id]/comp/route.ts:275, .../void/route.ts:227, .../api/payments/refund/route.ts:423. After both branches merge to main, every 5.4.2 call site will fail TS compilation: (a) extra positional `supabase` arg, (b) missing required `actor` field, (c) `approved_by_user_id` is not a known property (5.4.3 names it `manager_pin_user_id`), (d) action strings `order_void`, `order_comp`, `order_void_after_close`, `order_comp_after_close`, `payment_partially_refunded` are NOT members of the AuditAction union (5.4.3 only declares `order_voided`, `order_comped`, `payment_refunded`).
issues.suggested_fix: Either (A) change 5.4.3's audit.record to accept the supabase-client-first signature 5.4.2 already ships AND rename `manager_pin_user_id` to `approved_by_user_id` AND extend AuditAction to include the verbs 5.4.2 uses (`order_void`, `order_comp`, `order_void_after_close`, `order_comp_after_close`, `payment_partially_refunded`); OR (B) coordinate a rename PR against 5.4.2's three call sites to match 5.4.3 (drop the supabase arg, wrap fields under `actor`, rename `approved_by_user_id`->`manager_pin_user_id`, change action verbs to past tense). Recommend (B) — 5.4.3's typed-action union and AuthUser-based actor are stricter and the right long-term API; 5.4.2's stub at src/lib/audit/log.ts (Owned by sister batch 5.4.3) was provisional. Whichever path is chosen, INTEGRATE.sh must apply the fix before merging the second of the two batches or main will not compile.

issues.problem: Page calls GET /api/staff to populate the actor/manager dropdowns, but checks neither response shape variation nor handles missing data field. If /api/staff returns a different envelope shape, dropdowns silently empty (best-effort path is acceptable but a console.warn would help diagnose).
issues.suggested_fix: Add a console.warn when staffRes.ok && body.data is undefined.

issues.problem: userNameCache is a module-level Map that grows unbounded across requests in a long-lived Node process (Next.js standalone). Multi-tenant deploys may cache thousands of entries; no eviction.
issues.suggested_fix: Cap the cache (LRU) or add a TTL. Not blocking — audit volume is low — but worth flagging for V7 reliability.

summary: State machine itself is excellent (8 states, ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS, IllegalTransitionError, 20/20 vitest tests pass, build passes, xstate ^5.31.0 added) and routes correctly enforce auth + manager-PIN + Zod + tenant scoping; FAIL is driven by 3 P0 cross-task signature mismatches (assertVersion, bumpVersion, audit.record + AuditAction enum) — every comp/void/refund route will TS-error and runtime-fail at integration when the real 5.4.1 + 5.4.3 helpers replace the stubs.

issues.problem: assertVersion() call site signature is incompatible with the real 5.4.1 helper. 5.4.2 stub takes (supabase, table:string, id, expectedVersion:number|null) and returns {ok, current_version, current_state}. Real 5.4.1 (../v5-batch-5.4.1-optimistic-locking/src/lib/orders/concurrency.ts:189) takes (supabase, request:Request, orderId, orgId, options?) and returns {ok:true, expectedVersion, currentRow, currentVersion} | {ok:false, response:NextResponse}. After INTEGRATE.sh merges the real 5.4.1, the comp/void/refund routes will fail TS compilation: wrong arg count, wrong arg types, no `current_version` / `current_state` props on the result. Same call site bug at void/route.ts:107 and payments/refund/route.ts:236. The refund route additionally passes table='payments' but real 5.4.1 only supports the orders table.
issues.suggested_fix: Pre-merge: edit the three routes to match the real signature: `const check = await assertVersion(supabase, request, orderId, user.org_id); if (!check.ok) return check.response;` then use check.expectedVersion / check.currentRow. For payments/refund/route.ts replace assertVersion with a direct payments-table version check (or add a payments variant in 5.4.1 before merge). Either fix here OR have the runner block 5.4.2 merge until 5.4.1 lands and add an integration-fixup commit.

issues.problem: bumpVersion() call site signature is incompatible with the real 5.4.1 helper. 5.4.2 stub is sync `bumpVersion<T>(updates: T): T` used inline as `.update(bumpVersion({status:'served',...}))`. Real 5.4.1 (concurrency.ts:346) is async `bumpVersion(supabase, orderId, orgId): Promise<void>` that performs its own UPDATE and returns nothing. After merge, every `.update(bumpVersion({...}))` call will pass a Promise<void> to Supabase's update() — TS error AND runtime corruption. Same bug at comp/route.ts:234, void/route.ts:169, payments/refund/route.ts:299, payments/refund/route.ts:385.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the bumpVersion(...) wrapper around update payloads — 5.4.1's design is for the BEFORE-UPDATE Postgres trigger (migration 20260504063720) to auto-increment version on any orders UPDATE. Replace `bumpVersion({...updates})` with just `{...updates}`. Add a TODO that any post-merge route doing INSERT-only on a child table without touching orders should call the real `bumpVersion(supabase, orderId, orgId)` to invalidate cached versions.

issues.problem: audit.record() signature AND action vocabulary are incompatible with the real 5.4.3 helper. 5.4.2 stub: `audit.record(supabase, {org_id, user_id, approved_by_user_id, action:string, ...})`. Real 5.4.3 (../v5-batch-5.4.3-audit-log/src/lib/audit/log.ts:187): `audit.record({actor:AuthUser, manager_pin_user_id, action:AuditAction, ...})` — no supabase param, takes typed `actor` not loose org_id/user_id, action is a strict union. Strings emitted by 5.4.2 routes — 'order_comp', 'order_comp_after_close', 'order_void', 'order_void_after_close', 'payment_partially_refunded' — are NOT in 5.4.3's AuditAction enum (which has 'order_comped', 'order_voided', 'payment_refunded'). After merge: TS errors on all 3 routes' audit.record calls + invalid action strings rejected by enum. Field renames: approved_by_user_id → manager_pin_user_id; supabase param removed; org_id/user_id → actor.
issues.suggested_fix: Pre-merge: rewrite all 3 audit.record call sites: drop first arg, replace {org_id:user.org_id, user_id:user.id, approved_by_user_id:m} with {actor:user, manager_pin_user_id:m}. Map action strings to the 5.4.3 AuditAction enum (order_comp→order_comped; order_comp_after_close→order_comped (with reason='after_close'); order_void→order_voided; order_void_after_close→order_voided; payment_partially_refunded→payment_refunded with metadata flag). Pass `request` to capture IP/UA. OR coordinate with 5.4.3 author to extend AuditAction with the new variants before merge.

issues.problem: Calls assertVersion(supabase, 'payments', payment_id, expectedVersion) but real 5.4.1 helper is hard-coded to load from `orders` table (concurrency.ts:138 `loadOrderForVersionCheck` → `.from('orders')`). Even if the wrapper were updated, the underlying loader will read an orders row by payment_id and 404, breaking every refund. Sister 5.4.1 doesn't add payments.version columns either (its migration is add_order_version_columns.sql per spec).
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) drop optimistic locking from the refund route and rely on payments.status='captured'|'settled' to prevent double-refunds (acceptable — payment refund races are processor-dedup'd by Valor's idempotency keys), or (b) add a separate payments.version column + helper in a coordination commit with 5.4.1 author. Option (a) is the lower-risk fix.

issues.problem: Comp route reads order columns `total, amount_paid, balance_due, closed_at` then later reads `total, amount_paid, balance_due` again at line 213 and `*` at line 293. Three separate round-trips for what could be a single SELECT * with the post-mutation refresh batched. Acceptable for correctness; visible latency on a busy POS comp flow.
issues.suggested_fix: Combine the post-mutation refresh + final response select into one .select('*, order_items(*, order_item_modifiers(*))') call. Drop the line 213 select since the same fields are in the final select.

issues.problem: Stub uses `(supabase.from('audit_log') as any).insert(...)` with eslint-disable to bypass type narrowing. Acceptable in a stub but the comment doesn't reference a tracking task ID per reviewer protocol.
issues.suggested_fix: Already documented as 5.4.3-owned; add an explicit TODO(5.4.3) on the eslint-disable line so it's grep-able from the integration cleanup pass.

issues.problem: State machine's CLOSE branch in the pure switch (line 105-106) returns 'served' if balance_due_cents > 0, while the XState machine (line 200-212) does the same. Correct, but the `nextState()` semantics ('CLOSE on positive balance' is a legal transition that returns 'served', i.e. a no-op state change) may confuse future callers — looks like the call succeeded when really nothing moved. Tests pass but the asymmetry between 'illegal -> throws' and 'no-op -> silently returns same state' is a footgun.
issues.suggested_fix: Either (a) treat CLOSE-with-positive-balance as illegal (return null / throw) so callers must explicitly handle the 'still owe' branch, or (b) add a doc comment to nextState explaining that some transitions are intentional self-edges. (a) is the cleaner contract.

summary: Migration + trigger applied to Supabase; 14 routes wired with assertVersion; StaleOrderModal+mutateOrder complete. Build/lint clean. Two real concerns: (1) 5.4.1's assertVersion/bumpVersion signatures are INCOMPATIBLE with 5.4.2's stub call sites — comp/void routes will fail to compile after merge; (2) several routes do the version check but defer the actual bump to recalculateOrderTotals's unconditional UPDATE, widening the TOCTOU window.

issues.problem: 5.4.2's worktree (.claude/worktrees/v5-batch-5.4.2-state-machine/src/app/api/orders/[id]/{comp,void}/route.ts) calls assertVersion(supabase, 'orders', orderId, expectedVersion) expecting {ok, current_version, current_state}, and bumpVersion({...updates}) as a synchronous dict transformer. 5.4.1's real API is assertVersion(supabase, request, orderId, orgId, options?) and bumpVersion(supabase, orderId, orgId) async. After merge, 5.4.2's comp/void routes will not compile.
issues.suggested_fix: Either: (a) add backwards-compat overloads to concurrency.ts that match 5.4.2's stub shape, OR (b) the runner must update 5.4.2's comp/void/walkout routes during INTEGRATE.sh to call the real API (read request header, pass orgId, branch on check.ok/check.response, gate UPDATE with .eq('version', check.expectedVersion), use checkUpdateAffectedRow afterward). Option (b) is the right one — the stub's API is wrong.

issues.problem: assertVersion runs before items insert, but the order-row UPDATE that triggers the version bump happens inside recalculateOrderTotals via an unconditional UPDATE (no .eq('version', expectedVersion), no checkUpdateAffectedRow). A concurrent writer that moves the version between assertVersion's SELECT and recalculateOrderTotals's UPDATE will silently win. Same pattern in items/[itemId]/route.ts (PATCH+DELETE), discount/route.ts, fire-course/route.ts, merge/route.ts, split/route.ts, auto-gratuity/route.ts.
issues.suggested_fix: Either thread expectedVersion through recalculateOrderTotals so it can gate its UPDATE on the version (and re-run/409 if zero rows updated), or perform an explicit conditional UPDATE on orders before recalculateOrderTotals runs and use checkUpdateAffectedRow. Document the deliberately-loose semantics if accepted as-is — the assertVersion check is currently advisory for these 7 routes.

issues.problem: DELETE handler (void via DELETE verb) bypasses assertVersion entirely — it goes SELECT status → UPDATE status='voided' with no If-Match check. If a client uses the DELETE-style void path concurrently with a server's mutation, last-write wins.
issues.suggested_fix: Add assertVersion gate at top of DELETE handler matching the PATCH pattern (or document that DELETE is a deliberate fast-path because void is terminal).

issues.problem: Comment says offline replay does NOT thread version (intentional) so the server accepts buffered writes. This contradicts the spec's promise that all 13 routes are gated — offline-replayed mutations bypass optimistic locking. Reasonable trade-off but should be flagged for V5.4.1 follow-up.
issues.suggested_fix: No code change needed; either add a TODO referencing the offline-replay version-tracking work or accept the documented trade-off.

summary: Migration installs custom_access_token_hook per spec: SECURITY DEFINER + search_path='', EXECUTE locked to supabase_auth_admin only, null-row guard for deleted/incomplete users, top-level org_id claim merged so 209 baseline policies resolve correctly, rollback paired and correct, build+lint clean (0 errors), MCP apply_migration confirmed on lbekiyxqemxozmghgmtp with live dry-run.

issues.problem: Comment says SECURITY DEFINER runs as postgres 'so we don't need to relax users RLS for the auth hook role' — but step 4 immediately adds the auth_hook_read_users RLS policy for supabase_auth_admin anyway. The SQL is correct (postgres BYPASSRLS is set in Supabase so the body executes regardless), but the comment contradicts what follows and may confuse future maintainers debugging the chicken-and-egg concern.
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite the comment: explain that SECURITY DEFINER as postgres would bypass RLS on its own, and that the step-4 policy is explicit defense-in-depth so the hook still works if someone ever strips BYPASSRLS from the postgres role, and to match Supabase canonical docs. The policy is not harmful and should be kept.

issues.problem: REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC is sufficient to cover anon and authenticated since both inherit from PUBLIC; the separate REVOKE FROM anon, authenticated on the next line is redundant (correct behavior but dead statement).
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the redundant `REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.custom_access_token_hook(jsonb) FROM anon, authenticated;` line, or leave it as belt-and-suspenders with a comment noting the redundancy.

issues.problem: mapVoidReasonToEnum maps label "Long wait time" (VoidReasonDialog id: long_wait) to enum value "kitchen_error". Long wait is a customer dissatisfaction reason, not a kitchen preparation error. Audit logs and analytics will misclassify these voids.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the l.includes("long wait") branch to return "customer_request" (closest semantic match in the existing enum), or add "long_wait" to the VOID_REASONS enum in void/route.ts and the Zod schema.

issues.problem: Stale comment: "Draft voids by anyone are handled by DELETE /api/orders/[id]" — that handler was removed by this task (5.99.3). The comment now points to a non-existent route and will mislead future engineers.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove or rewrite the parenthetical to describe the current behavior: all voids (including draft-order voids) now go through this POST /void endpoint.

branch: main (direct commit b35c598 — worktree isolation failure)
summary: All 5 acceptance criteria met cleanly (vitest.config.ts scoped, INTEGRATE.sh EXIT trap + dirty-check + here-string + npm test first gate, DEPLOY.sh PREV_COMMIT + rollback + pm2 describe + rm-rf+cp + .env.local preserved, ci.yml no auto-deploy, .gitattributes union); two P1 edge-case gaps in the rollback path and a process violation (commit on main instead of worktree branch).

issues.problem: /tmp/sear_prev_commit is written AFTER pm2 save (line 84). If the SSH session crashes or the VM OOMs between pm2 save and the echo, the rollback SSH block finds no /tmp/sear_prev_commit, prints 'manual intervention required', and exits the conditional without error — while prod is left running broken code. The JSONL entry still logs smoke_failed_rolled_back which implies rollback occurred.
issues.suggested_fix: Move `echo "PREV_COMMIT=$PREV_COMMIT" > /tmp/sear_prev_commit` to immediately after line 55 (right after capturing PREV_COMMIT, before git pull). That way it is always present before the deployment mutates anything. Also rename the JSONL status to smoke_failed_rollback_attempted vs smoke_failed_rolled_back to distinguish success from failure.

issues.problem: Rollback SSH block runs set -euo pipefail. If npm run build fails during rollback (disk space, corrupt deps), the SSH exits non-zero but the outer local script has no explicit check on the SSH exit code — set -e on the local side will catch it and terminate before exit 1. However the JSONL record (line 135) is written unconditionally and says smoke_failed_rolled_back regardless of whether the rollback build/reload succeeded. Ops will see smoke_failed_rolled_back in the log and assume prod is safe when it may still be broken.
issues.suggested_fix: Capture the rollback SSH exit code: `rollback_ok=0; ssh ... || rollback_ok=$?`. Then emit different JSONL status: smoke_failed_rollback_ok vs smoke_failed_rollback_failed. Exit non-zero in both cases but surface which one for on-call clarity.

issues.problem: npm run test:e2e still hits prod URL (playwright.config.ts baseURL=https://getsear.com). Pre-deploy integration tests validate old prod, not the new build. Not in scope for 5.99.8 (it was F-07/P1 in the original review) but the implementer did not document this as a known remaining gap.
issues.suggested_fix: Track as a follow-up in the next batch; add a comment in INTEGRATE.sh noting the baseURL limitation so reviewers are not surprised.

issues.problem: Agent committed directly to local main (commit b35c598) instead of isolating work in a worktree branch. This bypasses the branch-based review gate the worktree system is designed to enforce. The branch field in this review record reflects the anomaly.
issues.suggested_fix: Runner should verify worktree isolation before merging; agents must not have write access to main directly. Consider adding a pre-commit hook that rejects commits on main made by builder@aiviizn.com.

summary: All 6 migration issues addressed correctly across 4 forward migrations and 4 paired rollbacks; build green; no project-rule violations.

issues.problem: Rollback restores allow_update WITH CHECK (true) but the baseline policy (line 4658 of 00000000000000_baseline.sql) has only USING (true) with no WITH CHECK clause. The restored policy is slightly stricter than the original, which is harmless in practice but not a byte-for-byte rollback to prior state.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the rollback allow_update to match the baseline exactly: CREATE POLICY "allow_update" ON public.campaign_recipients FOR UPDATE USING (true);

issues.problem: VALIDATE CONSTRAINT runs unconditionally outside the DO/IF NOT EXISTS block. If the constraint was added by the DO block in this run, VALIDATE proceeds correctly. However if the migration is applied a second time (replay scenario), the DO block skips the ADD CONSTRAINT but VALIDATE still fires — this is a no-op if the constraint is already valid, so no error, but the intent-guard comment implies idempotency that is only partially true.
issues.suggested_fix: Wrap the VALIDATE in its own IF EXISTS check mirroring the NOT VALID block, or add a comment noting that VALIDATE on an already-valid constraint is a harmless no-op in Postgres (which it is).

summary: All 5 P0 schema/idempotency fixes are correctly implemented and build is green, but the recipients POST route at line 87 uses a bare type assertion instead of Zod to parse the customer_ids body — individual UUID elements go unvalidated to the DB upsert, violating the project Zod-at-boundaries rule (P1).

issues.problem: POST body is parsed via `body as { customer_ids?: string[] }` with only a manual Array.isArray check. Individual customer_id elements are never validated as UUIDs via Zod. A malformed string (e.g. SQL-injection attempt, excessively long string, non-uuid) is forwarded directly to the Supabase upsert. CLAUDE.md requires Zod at all API system boundaries. DB will 500 on a malformed UUID (22P02) but the error message leaks schema info and there is no client-facing validation message.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the manual check with a Zod schema: `const recipientsBodySchema = z.object({ customer_ids: z.array(z.string().uuid()).min(1).max(500) }); const parsed = recipientsBodySchema.safeParse(body);` and gate the rest of the handler on `parsed.success`. The max(500) cap also prevents unbounded batch inserts.

issues.problem: File is created in the project root, violating CLAUDE.md rule 'NEVER save scratch/working files to the project root'. The spec required the file to exist but did not specify root — docs/ is the correct home for coordination notes. The existing root already has 30+ .md files (pre-existing tech debt) but new files should not compound that.
issues.suggested_fix: Move to docs/MARKETING_MIGRATION_NEEDED.md or docs/migrations/MARKETING_MIGRATION_NEEDED.md to follow the file organization rules.

issues.problem: Four `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` suppressions are added without a TODO comment citing a tracking task ID, as required by CLAUDE.md. Same pattern was pre-existing in the file and across the marketing module, but new suppressions should not perpetuate the anti-pattern.
issues.suggested_fix: Add `// TODO(5.99.x): remove after Supabase JS v3 ships proper generics` after each disable comment, or type the Supabase client query chain explicitly to eliminate the need.

summary: All 5 P0 surfaces are addressed and build/tests pass, but manager self-authorization in payments/void bypasses the 'ALWAYS require PIN' invariant, auth_login_rate_limited enum is dead code (login 429 path writes no audit row), and eslint-disable comments lack required TODO+task-ID per CLAUDE.md.

issues.problem: Manager self-authorization path (isManagerRole && !manager_pin → managerPinUserId = user.id) lets any role=manager session void a payment of any amount without entering a PIN. Spec criterion says manager-PIN ALWAYS required regardless of amount or role. A compromised manager session or insider with borrowed badge can void without any physical PIN input; the only audit evidence is their own user_id, which is circular.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the isManagerRole && !manager_pin shortcut. Always call validateManagerPin(supabase, user.org_id, manager_pin) and require the manager_pin field to be present. Managers authenticating their own actions is fine but they must still supply the PIN so the hardware is in their hands.

issues.problem: auth_login_rate_limited is declared in the AuditAction union but is never called anywhere. The auth/login 429 rate-limit path returns silently without writing an audit row. The declared enum value is dead code; the audit trail for credential-stuffing detection the criterion implies is absent.
issues.suggested_fix: In src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts, call audit.record({action:'auth_login_rate_limited', actor: {id:'anonymous', org_id:'', ...}, entity_type:'auth', entity_id:email, description:'Login rate-limited', reason:'ip_or_email_exhaustion', request}) before returning the 429. Note: audit.record requires an AuthUser-shaped actor — pass a placeholder or extend the helper to accept null actor for pre-auth contexts.

issues.problem: Multiple eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any directives throughout manager-pin.ts and staff/checkout/route.ts lack required TODO comment + tracking task ID per CLAUDE.md project rules. Violates the stated rule: '@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any without a TODO comment + tracking task ID'.
issues.suggested_fix: Add // TODO(5.99.x): replace any with typed Supabase client once createAdminClient returns a typed QueryBuilder — tracking task after each eslint-disable line, or type the supabase parameter as SupabaseClient from @supabase/supabase-js.

issues.problem: Per-org rate-limit uses checkRateLimit('auth', orgKey) which applies the auth-tier limit of 5/15min, not the 10/15min documented in the comment ('10 attempts / 15 min — pin-verify tier'). The comment is misleading: the effective org limit is 5, not 10. Being more restrictive is safer but the mismatch between documented and actual limit will cause confusion when operators expect 10 org-wide attempts and only get 5.
issues.suggested_fix: Either update the comment to reflect 5/15min, or add a dedicated 'pin-verify' tier to TIER_CONFIGS in src/lib/api/rate-limit.ts at {limit:10, windowSeconds:900} and call checkRateLimit('pin-verify', orgKey).

summary: expectedVersion threaded correctly through all 9 call sites (8 routes + 1 function); version-gated UPDATE + StaleVersionError + 409 path all wired end-to-end; build and tests green; no scope creep into 5.99.3 or 5.99.4 territory.

issues.problem: In the StaleVersionError catch block, checkUpdateAffectedRow is called with recalcExpected (which is expectedVersion+1 for isAfterClose) as the expected_version argument. The 409 body sent to the client will say expected_version: N+1 rather than the original If-Match version N. The client StaleOrderModal likely uses this to display a diff, so the mismatch may confuse the UI — the client expects to see its own original version (N) as the expected version, not the intermediate post-reopen version.
issues.suggested_fix: Pass versionCheck.expectedVersion (the original If-Match value) rather than recalcExpected into checkUpdateAffectedRow's expectedVersion argument in the comp catch block. The 409 body will then match what the client sent, which is what StaleOrderModal expects.

issues.problem: The DELETE handler passes expectedVersion=null explicitly (correct — no If-Match guard yet), but the comment says 'deferred to sister 5.4.2' which does not match the task numbering scheme (should be 5.99.3). Minor but could confuse the next reviewer matching comments to task IDs.
issues.suggested_fix: Update comment to reference '5.99.3' to match the actual task ID in the build pipeline.
